clue.text: Drops a line about noisy ceremonies

indicators.note: noisy tells us the ceremonies are to be taken as a spoken sound, not as written

parts.note: rites are religious or formal ceremonies

explanation.surface: Someone sends a short letter complaining about loud rituals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word here; 'noisy' is the sound signal, so RITES heard aloud gives a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop someone a line is an idiom for sending them a short letter, which is corresponding with them on paper.

clue.text: Bypass group on the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes first, above it

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring
a road is a way, a route for travel

explanation.surface: A gang gathered on a street, avoiding something.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypass is a road that circles a town so traffic avoids its centre, the usual British term being a ring road.

clue.text: He paints badly — can he act?

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A poor painter wonders whether he might be any better on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the eight letters of HE PAINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is an actor, from Thespis, the supposed first performer of Greek tragedy, so the question asks about a stage performer.

clue.text: Celebrity gives autograph to Leo and the twins

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a famous person signs when giving an autograph

explanation.surface: A famous person signs a book for a fan called Leo and two twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo and the twins (Gemini) look like people meeting a celebrity; they are signs of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo and Gemini are examples of zodiac signs, which are the twelve astrological divisions of the year.

clue.text: Dogs stagger badgers? Not bad, not good either!

parts.note: to lurch is to stagger

indicators.note: not good either says the abbreviation for good is also taken away from what is left
Not tells us the word bad is to be taken away from badgers

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dogs reeling about, and badgers that are neither bad nor good.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing BAD from BADGERS leaves GERS; removing G then leaves ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, usually part greyhound, so lurchers are a kind of hound.

clue.text: Moving, thrilling — take an imaginative leap

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted about, so the words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exciting, stirring jump of the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges the fifteen letters of THRILLING TAKE AN; 'Moving' and 'thrilling' both read as praise in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking is solving problems by an indirect, creative approach, which is a jump of imagination rather than step-by-step logic.

clue.text: Infection found in capital of central Lahore, spreading

indicators.note: the capital, the head letter, of the word central is taken
spreading means the letters of Lahore are spread out and reordered

explanation.surface: A disease is discovered in the heart of Lahore and is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts a reading about Lahore as a city; it gives the C of 'central'. 'spreading' rearranges LAHORE into HOLERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute bacterial disease of the gut caught from contaminated water, so it is an infection.

clue.text: Trader in old ale

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
porter is a dark beer, a type of ale

explanation.surface: A merchant who deals in an old beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter sells goods abroad, so is a merchant or dealer.

clue.text: Hit and run — that's careless

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver shows recklessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means done hastily and sloppily, without proper care.

clue.text: Play ones part quietly, subject to law

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under orders
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: An actor performs softly because some regulation demands it.
explanation.definitionFit: To underact is to perform a role with restraint, playing it down rather than overdoing it.

clue.text: A bear coming back to west coast city is fair game

indicators.note: coming back means the word a and the bear are read backwards together

parts.note: Pooh is the bear of the Winnie-the-Pooh stories
LA is Los Angeles, on the US west coast

explanation.surface: A bear returns to Los Angeles, a legitimate target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns A POOH into HOOPA. 'fair game' looks like the idiom for a legitimate target; it means a game at a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a fairground stall where players throw rings over prizes, a game at a funfair.

clue.text: One might give her a ring

definitions.text: One might give her a ring

parts.words: One might give her a ring
parts.note: the surface suggests a phone call; the real sense is offering an engagement ring with a request to marry

explanation.surface: Somebody who might telephone a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give her a ring' reads as British slang for phoning her; the ring is an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A man asking for a woman's hand in marriage offers her an engagement ring, so he is the one popping the question.

clue.text: Had misgivings, listener having eaten outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for having eaten goes round the listener

parts.note: fed means having eaten
an ear is the organ one listens with

explanation.surface: Someone was uneasy after an eavesdropper dined out in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten outside' looks like dining al fresco, but 'outside' is the container signal and 'having eaten' is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Feared means was afraid or worried, which is having misgivings about something.

clue.text: Innocent — and a plant!

parts.note: angelic means innocent, like an angel

explanation.surface: Something pure, and a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelica is an aromatic herb whose candied stems decorate cakes, a flowering species of the carrot family.

clue.text: Chicken and cow are heard to die

definitions.note: chicken is a noun here for lack of nerve, as when someone shows chicken

indicators.note: heard tells us cow are is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: the words cow are, said together, sound like the start of the answer
a die is one of a set of dice, and in modern use dice serves as the singular too

explanation.surface: A hen and a cow are said to be facing death.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter treats DIE loosely as DICE; said aloud, 'cow are' plus DICE gives the whole word. 'Chicken' looks like a farm animal beside the cow; it is the slang sense of being timid.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for cowardly fear, a lack of courage, from the bird's reputation as timid.

clue.text: The god of war makes no noise

parts.note: O is zero, nothing, so it stands for no
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A warrior deity moves silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes no noise' reads as silence; O and DIN are pieces joined by 'makes'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the chief god was associated with war, wisdom and death, ruling Asgard.

clue.text: Biased, like mobius' band

definitions.meaning: biased means partial, favouring one party
a Möbius band is a twisted loop of paper with a single surface

explanation.surface: Prejudiced, like a famous twisted mathematical loop.
explanation.walkthrough: A Möbius strip is a band given a half-twist before joining its ends, so it has only one surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A biased account favours one party unfairly; a Möbius band famously has a single surface and edge.

clue.text: The distinctive marks in a gin cocktail? Yes, in Spain, inside

indicators.note: inside means the Spanish yes goes into the mixed letters
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of in a gin are mixed

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes

explanation.surface: Emblems found in a gin drink, approved in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges the six letters of 'in a gin', and 'inside' places the Spanish word within them after the second letter; the first 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or emblems showing rank or membership, identifying symbols worn or displayed.

clue.text: Shrewd, missing first of the month

indicators.note: missing first of says the opening letter of the month is dropped

parts.note: March is a month

explanation.surface: Clever, but absent at the start of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the month' must be a particular month, MARCH, whose first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means knowing or cunning, as in an arch smile, which is sly and astute.

clue.text: Officer and worker supporting a day project

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting others sits below them, so it comes last

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
the ant is the stock crossword worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: A military man and a labourer back a one-day scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' is a verb, to stick out, not a noun for a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a staff officer who assists a commanding officer with administration.

clue.text: Arrive with fluffy hair, in disappointment

parts.note: to come is to arrive
down is fine soft hair or feathers

explanation.surface: Turning up with frizzy hair is a let-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a decline or anticlimax, a let-down after high hopes.

clue.text: Rejected less inside, and ate

indicators.note: inside takes just the inner letters of the word less, dropping its first and last

parts.note: chewed means ate, worked food in the mouth

explanation.surface: Someone turned down smaller portions indoors, then ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to avoid or abstain from, so eschewed means shunned or turned down.

clue.text: Resolutions in lent are timeless

indicators.note: resolutions here are re-solvings, so the letters of lent are are worked out anew

explanation.surface: Lenten resolutions last for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolutions' looks like Lenten vows; it rearranges LENT ARE, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever, without beginning or end, outside time.

clue.text: The famous cook's back, having gone by yacht

indicators.note: back means the cook's name with its possessive is read in reverse

parts.note: Delia Smith is Britain's best-known TV cookery writer, so the famous cook's is Delia's

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef returns after a boating trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a hugely popular British TV cook; DELIAS reversed gives the answer. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail is to travel by boat under canvas, so travelling by yacht means one sailed.

clue.text: Cultivated about rude turn

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grew coarse after a rude change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of RUDE TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture is to rear or tend something so it grows, as a gardener cultivates plants.

clue.text: Noise at home starting to grate, when having a meal

parts.note: din is a loud noise
in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: starting to takes the opening letter of the word grate

explanation.surface: A clatter at home starts to irritate at mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' reads as annoying; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining means eating dinner, which is sitting down to a meal.

clue.text: Playing at it, miro is an impressionist

indicators.note: playing about with letters means rearranging them, so at it miro is shuffled

explanation.surface: Joan Miró is at work, a painter of the Impressionist kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges AT IT MIRO. Miró, a Spanish painter, makes 'impressionist' look like the art movement; it means a mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: An impressionist is an entertainer who mimics famous people, someone who copies voices and mannerisms.

clue.text: Student in art is lengthening his vowels

indicators.note: in means the student goes inside the word for art

parts.note: drawing is an art
L is the learner driver's plate, so it stands for a student

explanation.surface: An art student speaks slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawling means speaking slowly with drawn-out sounds, stretching the syllables.

clue.text: Range times 10 in case of eyesight

indicators.note: in puts the multiplication sign and ten within the shell of eyesight
the case of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
ten is the number 10

explanation.surface: Ten times better vision, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' is the X multiplication sign; E...T is the first and last letters of 'eyesight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is scope or reach, how far something covers, the span of it.
